intro: KM1-1 Hase Lanes as the game now builds it (Kamakura's own level, in its own scene, not yet shown to players): every model you approved, the sixteen plants and pots from your plant views, the home at the door and Hase Station at the stop, read from the level's code and rendered through the game camera. Where a picture is still to come, a plain box stands in: the lane's houses (from your lane pictures KM1-1a to e), the block wall and the wooden fence.
reference: KM1-1 Hase Lanes, the photographic version the models were built from.
strip: Screen by screen as the game camera frames it (about 10 m back, 3.1 m above and below the lane at 16:9). The pink post and the white cube are the kid and the ball, for scale. The shading is Blender's, not the game's toon look.
decided: The level is its own scene, KM1-1_HaseLanes_KM, beside the original town's 23 levels, and not in the menus yet: Kamakura's routes are switched on together (BUILD KM-L99).

Everything beside the lane stands 0.75 m further back than in the proposed layout: the game's footpath, where the kid plays, is 1.5 m either side of the lane, the layout's green strip 0.75 m. Nothing tall stands in front of the lane (LEARNINGS E10).
The first-graders walk in a loose line, slower than the kid, each its own short stretch: solid to the ball, the kid slips past.

The level crossing: the bells and lamps, the barriers coming down along the lane behind it (never toward the camera), and the tram coming down the tracks toward the camera and on over the road. On the rails while they flash, the ball is lost: "Ding ding! Wait for the barriers to go up".
The cat on the block wall is the game's cat until Kamakura's own animals (the ginger cat, the sparrows, the swallows, the crow) are put in the game.
ask: Redo when you can: the garden pine's TOP (KM-G15: its tree is built from its front and side meanwhile), and KM1-1c's corrugated house (its stand-in is a box).
Anything to move or change in the level: a model's place, the play, the length, the stand-ins' colours.
